articles.title: 8th Sunday of the Great Advent with the readings of 3rd Sunday of Advent, year A
paragraphs: Eighth week: the joy of Advent
Isaiah 35: 1-6a. 10

The desert and the parched land will exult; the steppe will rejoice and bloom. They will bloom with abundant flowers, and rejoice with joyful song. The glory of Lebanon will be given to them, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon; they will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God. Strengthen the hands that are feeble, make firm the knees that are weak, say to those whose hearts are frightened: Be strong, fear not! Here is your God, he comes with vindication; with divine recompense he comes to save you. Then will the eyes of the blind be opened, the ears of the deaf be cleared; then will the lame leap like a stag, then the tongue of the mute will sing.
Those whom the LORD has ransomed will return and enter Zion singing, crowned with everlasting joy; they will meet with joy and gladness, sorrow and mourning will flee.
The LORD God keeps faith forever,
secures justice for the oppressed,
gives food to the hungry.
The LORD sets captives free.
The LORD gives sight to the blind;
the LORD raises up those who were bowed down.
The LORD loves the just;
the LORD protects strangers.
The fatherless and the widow he sustains,
but the way of the wicked he thwarts.
The LORD shall reign forever;
your God, O Zion, through all generations.
James 5: 7-10

Be patient, brothers and sisters, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient with it until it receives the early and the late rains. You too must be patient. Make your hearts firm, because the coming of the Lord is at hand. Do not complain, brothers and sisters, about one another, that you may not be judged. Behold, the Judge is standing before the gates. Take as an example of hardship and patience, brothers and sisters, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
Matthew 11: 2-11

When John the Baptist heard in prison of the works of the Christ, he sent his disciples to Jesus with this question, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?" Jesus said to them in reply, "Go and tell John what you hear and see: the blind regain their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the good news proclaimed to them. And blessed is the one who takes no offense at me."

As they were going off, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John, "What did you go out to the desert to see? A reed swayed by the wind? Then what did you go out to see? Someone dressed in fine clothing? Those who wear fine clothing are in royal palaces. Then why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet. This is the one about whom it is written: Behold, I am sending my messenger ahead of you; he will prepare your way before you. Amen, I say to you, among those born of women there has been none greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he."
Questions:

- It is written in the book of prophet Isaiah: “Those whom the LORD has ransomed will return and enter Zion singing, crowned with everlasting joy; they will meet with joy and gladness, sorrow and mourning will flee.” – Do I see in my life the connection between faith and happiness, between God and joy?

- It is written in the Letter of Saint James: “Be patient, brothers and sisters, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient with it until it receives the early and the late rains.” – How do I experience the waiting for the fulfillment of something important to me? From what aspects (moments) of waiting can I learn ? What can I learn through a time of waiting?

- It is written in the Gospel: “When John the Baptist heard in prison of the works of the Christ, he sent his disciples to Jesus with this question, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?"” – Do I have the courage to ask priests or fellow community members difficult or simple questions? How can I, during times of doubt, become stronger and how can I try to clarify things which are unclear or uncertain?
Questions for children:

- It is written in the book of prophet Isaiah: “Those whom the LORD has ransomed will return and enter Zion singing, crowned with everlasting joy; they will meet with joy and gladness, sorrow and mourning will flee.” – Do I see in my life the connection between faith and happiness, between God and joy?

- It is written in the Letter of Saint James: “Be patient, brothers and sisters, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient with it until it receives the early and the late rains.” – What is the blessing (the good) of patience? How does patience affect us and what does it give us (teach us)?

- It is written in the Gospel: “When John the Baptist heard in prison of the works of the Christ, he sent his disciples to Jesus with this question, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?"” – Who do I talk to when I have doubts about faith or other matters? Do I try to present the questions to God in my prayers? Do I present them to my parents or to a priest or wise person in the community - people whom God gave to guide me?

articles.title: January 27 – Feast of Saint Angela Merici
articles.introduction: A docility to God lived in the small daily things, the Saint Pope Paul VI defined her as Apostle of modern times.
paragraphs: Angela Merici is born in Desenzano, on Lake Gardain Italy, around the year 1470 from a family of rural landowners. Since early childhood, she heard her father read the Bible or the lives of saints.

One day, still adolescent, during the break from the fields’ work, an episode happens that affects her entire life: Angela sees a ladder joining earth to heaven and a procession of angels and young women going up and down. She doesn’t comprehend the meaning of what she has seen, but keeps the fact to herself and is convinced that it must be a sign from God to her.

Angela’s life resumes. It peacefully flows between housework and the work in the fields: the French invasion, that at the beginning of the 15th century reaches Desenzano sowing death and destruction, offers to Angela an opportunity to dedicate herself totally to help and console those who lost all.

In 1516 Angela goes to Brescia: around her a large circle of people gather; women and men who look at her as a human and spiritual reference. However, she has not forgotten the vision of long ago and continues to question herself on what God wants from her: to get more light she makes pilgrimages to Milano, Roma and in the Holy Land.

She avails her wisdom to anyone in need whether of high or low condition; she has a wise word for all. In Venice and in Roma, Angela is asked to remain in order to organize the service to the poor but she prefers to go back to Brescia. She feels that God wants her there and there He will allow her to fulfill what He asks her to do.

During that time some young women start to gather around her. She shares the wish to offer to the women of her time the chance to be fully realized by giving themselves to the Lord in a new way, that is to continue living in their homes and among people, without being forced to embrace a cloistered life or to marry a man chosen by the parents. The vision of long ago is becoming real.
So, on November 25, 1535 she founds in Brescia the Company of Saint Orsola.
On January 27,1540, the Mother, as Angela is now called by all, dies contemplating face to face the God Whom she had recognized and loved in all those sisters and brothers.

Angela Merici spent forty years in Desenzano. Indeed, a very long time but not just for preparation to what will come after. We think of the Son of God who spent several years in Nazareth to listen and to learn by sharing life with common people. Angela spends her days between house and field work, listening to people, in prayer, studying and assimilating God’s Word. Thus, she becomes a profound knower of the human soul.

The docility to God lived in the small daily things has shaped the life of St. Angela. It allowed her to realize a new form of Consecrated life by which the contemplative dimension immersed her in the society for the apostolic action; her insight was so great and fundamental also for women’s emancipation that Saint Pope Paul VI defined Angela Merici Apostle of modern times.

articles.title: Lectures on Zoom about the Eucharist
articles.introduction: Next Monday (29.01), at 8.30.pm the St. James Vicariate will continue a series of lectures online about the Eucharist: "The Greatest Mystery of Our Life". The lecturers of the 16-lessons course are Rivka and fr. Piotr. Everyone is invited.
paragraphs: The lectures will guide the listeners through all the parts of the holy liturgy.
The topics of the lectures:

Introductory Rites (Entrance procession, Greeting, Penitential Act) Introductory Rites (Glory to God, Collect) Liturgy of the Word (First Reading, Responsorial Psalm, Second Reading, Gospel Acclamation) Liturgy of the Word (Gospel, Homily, Profession of Faith, Universal Prayer) Liturgy of the Eucharist (Presentation of the Gifts, Preparation of the Altar, Prayer over the Offerings) Eucharistic Prayer (Preface, Holy, Holy, Holy, First half of prayer, including Consecration) Eucharistic Prayer (Mystery of Faith, Second half of prayer, including Doxology, The Lord's Prayer) Communion (Sign of Peace, Lamb of God, Communion, Prayer after Communion), Concluding Rites (Greeting and Blessing, Dismissal)
Each topic will be commented by fr. Piotr and a week later by Rivka.
In order to participate in the lecture (Monday, at 20:30), please click the following link:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81111549071?pwd=S0kyMlpnUGdUbCtxaWd2WjVzNEp4UT09
The dates of the lectures:
The recorded lessons are available on our YouTube channel: HERE.

quarantine.title: 15th Sunday in Year A
quarantine.introduction: Every week, on our YouTube channel we publish a short movie about the Gospel of the week in the Hebrew language. Watch a short explanation of the Gospel-reading of today's Sunday. This week we read Mt 13:1-23. The teacher of this week is Fr. David.
paragraphs: You can watch the lesson: HERE.
Do not forget to subscribe to our YouTube channel.
מתי יג: 1-23

1בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יָצָא יֵשׁוּעַ מִן הַבַּיִת וְיָשַׁב עַל-יַד הַיָּם. 2כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּקְהֲלוּ אֵלָיו הֲמוֹן עַם רַב יָרַד לַסִּירָה לָשֶׁבֶת בָּהּ וְכָל הֶהָמוֹן עָמַד עַל הַחוֹף. 3אָז דִּבֵּר אֲלֵיהֶם רַבּוֹת בִּמְשָׁלִים וְאָמַר: "הִנֵּה הַזּוֹרֵעַ יָצָא לִזְרֹעַ. 4כַּאֲשֶׁר זָרַע נָפְלוּ כַּמָּה זְרָעִים בְּשׁוּלֵי הַדֶּרֶךְ וּבָאוּ צִפֳּרִים וְאָכְלוּ אוֹתָם. 5אֲחֵרִים נָפְלוּ עַל אַדְמַת טְרָשִׁים, בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהֶם הַרְבֵּה אֲדָמָה, וּמִהֲרוּ לִצְמֹחַ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהֶם אֲדָמָה עֲמֻקָּה. 6אוּלָם כְּשֶׁזָּרְחָה הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ נִצְרְבוּ וּבְאֵין שֹׁרֶשׁ הִתְיַבְּשׁוּ. 7אֲחֵרִים נָפְלוּ בֵּין קוֹצִים, אַךְ הַקּוֹצִים צָמְחוּ וְהֶחֱנִיקוּ אוֹתָם. 8וַאֲחֵרִים נָפְלוּ עַל אֲדָמָה טוֹבָה וְעָשׂוּ פְּרִי - זֶה פִּי מֵאָה, זֶה פִּי שִׁשִּׁים וְזֶה פִּי שְׁלוֹשִׁים. 9מִי שֶׁאָזְנַיִם לוֹ, שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע!" 10נִגְּשׁוּ הַתַּלְמִידִים וְשָׁאֲלוּ: "מַדּוּעַ אַתָּה מְדַבֵּר אֲלֵיהֶם בִּמְשָׁלִים?" 11הֵשִׁיב וְאָמַר: "מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלָּכֶם נִתַּן לָדַעַת אֶת סוֹדוֹת מַלְכוּת הַשָּׁמַיִם, אַךְ לָהֶם לֹא נִתַּן. 12כִּי מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ נָתוֹן יִנָּתֵן לוֹ וְשֶׁפַע יִהְיֶה לוֹ, אַךְ מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ, גַּם מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ יִלָּקַח מִמֶּנּוּ. 13לָכֵן בִּמְשָׁלִים אֲנִי מְדַבֵּר אֲלֵיהֶם, כִּי בִּרְאוֹתָם אֵינָם רוֹאִים וּבְשָׁמְעָם אֵינָם שׁוֹמְעִים אַף אֵינָם מְבִינִים. 14וּמִתְקַיֶּמֶת בָּהֶם נְבוּאַת יְשַׁעְיָהוּ לֵאמֹר: 'שִׁמְעוּ שָׁמוֹעַ וְאַל-תָּבִינוּ וּרְאוּ רָאוֹ וְאַל-תֵּדָעוּ. 15הַשְׁמֵן לֵב-הָעָם הַזֶּה וְאָזְנָיו הַכְבֵּד וְעֵינָיו הָשַׁע, פֶּן-יִרְאֶה בְעֵינָיו וּבְאָזְנָיו יִשְׁמָע וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין, וְשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ.' 16אַשְׁרֵי עֵינֵיכֶם הָרוֹאוֹת וְאָזְנֵיכֶם הַשּׁוֹמְעוֹת. 17אָמֵן. אוֹמֵר אֲנִי לָכֶם, נְבִיאִים וְצַדִּיקִים רַבִּים נִכְסְפוּ לִרְאוֹת אֶת אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם רוֹאִים וְלֹא רָאוּ, וְלִשְׁמֹעַ אֶת אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם שׁוֹמְעִים וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ." 18"וּבְכֵן שִׁמְעוּ אַתֶּם אֶת פֵּשֶׁר מְשַׁל הַזּוֹרֵעַ. 19כָּל הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ אֶת דְּבַר הַמַּלְכוּת וְאֵינֶנּוּ מֵבִין, בָּא הָרָע וְחוֹטֵף אֶת מַה שֶּׁנִּזְרַע בִּלְבָבוֹ; זֶהוּ הַנִּזְרָע בְּשׁוּלֵי הַדֶּרֶךְ. 20הַנִּזְרָע עַל אַדְמַת טְרָשִׁים הוּא הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ אֶת הַדָּבָר וּמִיָּד מְקַבֵּל אוֹתוֹ בְּשִׂמְחָה, 21אַךְ אֵין לוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ בְּתוֹכוֹ וְרַק לְשָׁעָה יַעֲמֹד, וּבִהְיוֹת צָרָה אוֹ רְדִיפָה בִּגְלַל הַדָּבָר הוּא נִכְשָׁל מִיָּד. 22הַנִּזְרָע בֵּין הַקּוֹצִים הוּא הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ אֶת הַדָּבָר, אֶלָּא שֶׁדַּאֲגוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּמַדּוּחֵי הָעֹשֶׁר מַחֲנִיקִים אֶת הַדָּבָר וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂה פְּרִי. 23הַנִּזְרָע עַל הָאֲדָמָה הַטּוֹבָה הוּא הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ אֶת הַדָּבָר וּמֵבִין וְגַם עוֹשֶׂה פְּרִי - זֶה עוֹשֶׂה פִּי מֵאָה, זֶה פִּי שִׁשִּׁים וְזֶה פִּי שְׁלוֹשִׁים."
